items.requirement: Produce all five required output files (q01.json, q02.json, q03.json, q04.json, q05.json) under /app/output/ as syntactically valid, non-empty JSON.
items.verification: A grader can verify this by loading each of the five files with a JSON parser and confirming the file exists, is non-empty, and parses without error.
items.notes: The instruction repeats an equivalent 'You are required to generate /app/output/qNN.json' sentence once per question (Q1–Q5); this item aggregates that recurring requirement.

items.requirement: Report a top-level ramp_rate_limit_c_per_s in q01.json equal to the maximum allowable preheat ramp rate defined in the handbook; for every run_id in mes_log.csv, compute max_preheat_ramp_c_per_s from thermocouples.csv restricted to the handbook-defined preheat temperature region, selecting the most representative thermocouple per the handbook, and record tc_id plus the value (or null if no valid preheat segment exists) under max_ramp_by_run; and list every run in violating_runs whose max_preheat_ramp_c_per_s exceeds the handbook's allowable ramp limit.
items.source_quote: Get the definition of preheat, the applicable temperature region, the ramp calculation equation, and the allowable limit from the handbook.
items.verification: A grader can verify this by: (1) reading ramp_rate_limit_c_per_s from q01.json and confirming it numerically matches the handbook's allowable preheat ramp limit; (2) recomputing, for each run, the maximum slope between consecutive thermocouple readings whose temperatures both fall inside the handbook preheat band, and confirming it matches the reported max_preheat_ramp_c_per_s (or null when no such segment exists); and (3) comparing each run's computed max preheat ramp against the allowable limit and confirming every run that exceeds it appears in violating_runs.
items.notes: Verifier only checks the top-level ramp_rate_limit_c_per_s field when it is present in the output; the output schema requires it regardless.

items.requirement: For each run_id in mes_log.csv, compute tal_s (time above the solder liquidus temperature, in seconds) from thermocouples.csv, and report it alongside run_id and tc_id in q02.json; derive required_min_tal_s and required_max_tal_s (the TAL window) from the handbook and set status to compliant when tal_s falls within that window, non-compliant otherwise; and sort the q02.json array so that entries are non-decreasing by run_id.
items.source_quote: Use the thermocouple data and solder liquidus temperature to calculate time above liquidus (TAL) in seconds for each run.
items.verification: A grader can verify this by: (1) re-integrating time-above-threshold (with linear interpolation at crossings) using each run's solder_liquidus_c from mes_log.csv and confirming it matches the reported tal_s for the run's representative thermocouple record; (2) checking that required_min_tal_s/required_max_tal_s match the handbook's stated TAL window and that status is 'compliant' exactly when required_min_tal_s <= tal_s <= required_max_tal_s; and (3) extracting the run_id sequence from q02.json and confirming it equals its own sorted version.

items.requirement: For each run_id, determine the required minimum peak temperature from the handbook (liquidus temperature plus the handbook's required margin) and report it with the run's lowest-peaking thermocouple's tc_id and peak_temp_c under min_peak_by_run; and list in failing_runs every run whose minimum peak temperature is below required_min_peak_c, including any run with no thermocouple data as failing.
items.source_quote: Check whether each run meets the peak temperature requirement.
items.verification: A grader can verify this by: (1) computing, per run, the maximum temp_c reached by each thermocouple, taking the thermocouple with the lowest such peak, and confirming reported peak_temp_c and required_min_peak_c match that value and the handbook-derived liquidus-plus-margin threshold; and (2) comparing the computed set of runs whose lowest thermocouple peak is below the required threshold (plus all runs lacking thermocouple data) against the failing_runs list and confirming they are identical sets.

items.requirement: For each run_id, derive required_min_speed_cm_min from the handbook's board geometry and thermal dwell requirements, and report it alongside the actual conveyor speed (actual_speed_cm_min) taken from mes_log.csv; set the boolean meets field to true if and only if actual_speed_cm_min is greater than or equal to required_min_speed_cm_min, for every run; and include exactly one entry per run_id from mes_log.csv in q04.json, sorted non-decreasing by run_id.
items.source_quote: Get board geometry, thermal dwell requirements, and allowable conveyor speed from the handbook.
items.verification: A grader can verify this by: (1) confirming actual_speed_cm_min equals the run's conveyor_speed_cm_min from mes_log.csv, and that required_min_speed_cm_min is a non-negative, plausible value consistent with the handbook's dwell/geometry-based formula; (2) checking meets is a JSON boolean and equals (actual_speed_cm_min >= required_min_speed_cm_min) for each run; and (3) confirming every run_id in mes_log.csv appears in q04.json and that the run_id sequence is sorted ascending.

items.requirement: For each distinct board_family present in mes_log.csv, output exactly one record naming a best_run_id that belongs to a run in that board_family, chosen by quality and efficiency; and list every remaining run_id of that board_family (i.e. all runs except best_run_id) in runner_up_run_ids, sorted ascending and not containing best_run_id.
items.source_quote: Select the best run per board_family based on quality and efficiency, and list other run_ids in runner_up_run_ids.
items.verification: A grader can verify this by: (1) confirming q05.json contains one record per unique board_family in mes_log.csv and that each best_run_id is a run_id actually belonging to that board_family; and (2) confirming runner_up_run_ids is sorted ascending, excludes best_run_id, and contains only run_ids belonging to the same board_family.
items.notes: Which specific run is 'best' depends on quality/efficiency signals (e.g., test_defects.csv, TAL/peak/ramp compliance) not fixed by the verifier beyond family membership.

items.requirement: Round every float value in q01.json–q05.json to 2 decimal places.
items.verification: A grader can verify this by parsing each numeric field across the five output files and confirming each equals its value rounded to at most 2 decimal places (no extra precision retained).

items.requirement: Use JSON null for any value that cannot be determined (e.g., a run with no thermocouple data) instead of fabricating a placeholder number.
items.verification: A grader can verify this by confirming that for any run lacking a valid preheat ramp segment, max_preheat_ramp_c_per_s is JSON null rather than a numeric value (as exercised for Q01), and spot-checking the same convention across Q02–Q05 outputs for runs missing underlying data.
items.notes: Only Q01 has an explicit verifier assertion for this null behavior; the same convention is expected but not separately asserted for Q02–Q05.

items.requirement: Base every handbook-derived constant or rule used in the answers (preheat region, ramp equation and limit, TAL definition/threshold/window, peak margin, conveyor speed formula, best-run criteria) on content actually present in handbook.pdf rather than assumed or invented values.
items.source_quote: Do not hallucinate or guess values.
items.verification: A grader can spot-check a sample of the numeric constants and formulas used across q01–q05 against the actual text of handbook.pdf to confirm they are directly sourced from it rather than generic or invented figures.
items.notes: This phrase recurs verbatim in each of the five questions; the grounding it demands is only partially checkable by the numeric-match assertions in the other items, so it is retained separately as a judge item.
